newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Elizabeth Taylor gets award for fight against AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Elizabeth Taylor gets award for fight against AIDS.

text.p: Actress Elizabeth Taylor on Monday received an award for courage from the group she helped found, the American Foundation for AIDS Research, known as AMFAR.
She told an special luncheon that people were under the illusion that she first became involved with AIDS because of the death of her friend, actor Rock Hudson.
But she said she had difficulties in 1984 when she organised her first AIDS benefit in Los Angeles, a time when no one wanted to speak publicly about the disease.
"I have never known rejection like that before in my life," she said. "Then Rock became sick and that really hit the town and people did start to get involved."
"I had no idea then I would be taking the first step on such a long and heartbreaking road," she said. "It isn't over yet. We need more than hope. We need you."
She was presented with a bracelet of hearts from the president of the Cartier jewelry firm, Simon Critchell, who quipped that Taylor had been "a long-time friend" of the company.

The day's events at the United Nations, following World AIDS Day on Sunday, were scheduled to culminate with speeches in the General Assembly hall by Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, Taylor and other speakers.
